name: Watsco, Inc.

listing.exchange: New York Stock Exchange (Common; Class B on NYSE American)

corporate_actions.event: Acquired Jackson's Supply (~$230m sales, 25 Sunbelt locations)
Completed acquisition of Granite Group (~$500m sales, 82 Northeast locations, HVAC + plumbing), funded from cash

geography.fx_notes: US ~90% of revenue with Sun Belt concentration; Canada, Latin America and Caribbean remainder (Morningstar profile via PitchBook). Split of the ~10% non-US between Canada and LatAm/Caribbean not extracted.

kpis.name: Mix
kpis.value: ~75-80% residential HVAC, 20-25% commercial; up to ~20% of US residential HVAC units distributed via Watsco; ~13% market share

company_fcf.definition: Operating cash flow (company highlights OCF, not FCF)

lease.source_id: US GAAP filer; operating leases in SG&A

acquisitions.notes: Jackson's Supply (~$230m sales) and Granite Group (~$500m sales); price not disclosed in source. Combined ~10% of revenue added.

management.cfo: Barry Logan (EVP; CFO role not re-verified)
management.senior_turnover_5y: Very low; A.J. (Aaron) Nahmad, President, son of CEO, leads technology strategy
management.succession_notes: Key-person/succession risk: long-serving founder-era CEO; family succession to A.J. Nahmad implied but not formally announced in sources

ownership.controlling_holders: Nahmad family: significant voting control via Class B shares (10 votes/share); exact % not verified this run
ownership.remuneration_notes: Long-dated restricted stock vesting at retirement ('ownership culture') - not re-verified
ownership.related_party: Carrier Enterprise JVs with Carrier Global (supplier and minority partner) - see sector notes

evidence: HVAC replacement is a necessity; installed base expanding [S1]
Residential replacement dominant vs new construction [S2]
A.rationale: Needs-based replacement demand with fragmented customers; weather and housing-cycle volatility.

evidence: Market leader ~13% share with largest network [S2]
B.rationale: Density, OEM exclusivity and contractor tools give a real advantage.

evidence: Op margin ~10% in a weak market
C.rationale: Scale benefits evident; GM gap to goal.

H.rationale: Weak minority protection on voting; noted neutrally.

sector_specific.notes: acquisition_growth_pct = Q3 2026 reported 7% less same-store 4% (ESTIMATE). Construction: new residential construction is a minority of residential sales (replacement majority) - share not extracted. Supplier concentration: Carrier is the dominant supplier and JV partner (Carrier Enterprise) - % of purchases not re-verified this run.

gates.notes: G3 -> B: supplier concentration on Carrier (dominant OEM and JV partner) - not a customer >15% but a single-supplier dependence; confirm % of purchases in 10-K. G1 net cash. H/dual-class noted neutrally.

bull_points: Net cash and steady roll-up (Jackson's, Granite add ~$730m sales) with plumbing adjacency (S1)
Replacement-driven demand with normalising conditions after A2L transition (S1)
Technology lead: e-commerce 37% of sales, OnCallAir GMV +14% (S1)
bear_points: Dual-class family control and long-tenured founder CEO succession risk (S4)
US Sun Belt concentration and housing/weather cyclicality (S2)
Dependence on Carrier as supplier/JV partner (S2)
thesis_breakers: Gross margin below 25% for a full year
Loss or restructuring of Carrier distribution rights
Same-store sales negative for 4 consecutive quarters outside a housing recession

sources.title: Watsco proxy statement / 10-K (capital structure: Common and Class B)
